summary.overview:
- Andrew Day leads the initiative for a holding company rollup of marketing agencies aimed at an 8 million EBITDA threshold for market sale.
- Six agencies show interest in the rollup but face hesitance, creating a catch-22 for first commitments needed.
- Substance Global, valued at 2.5 million EBITDA, is the largest target and focuses on transitioning from entertainment to pharma/wellness.
- Common Good, a 50-year-old family business with 1.4 million EBITDA, is apprehensive about rollup due to legacy concerns.
- Imaginary Content presenting over 1 million EBITDA is fully committed to the rollup, focusing on digital content for craft/retail brands.
- Current pipeline approaches 5 million EBITDA; requires an additional 3 million to meet the 8 million target for market readiness.
- Jon Simon is tasked with leading operational integration mapping of the agencies and identifying intellectual property assets.
- Holding company will utilize trigger contracts to buy companies at 5x multiples; equity distribution based on pro-rata valuations.
- External prospect Bulletproof Agency is being pursued for its international branding capabilities across multiple cities.
- Andrew Day to pitch to Common Good stakeholders, addressing emotional concerns before the financial considerations can be discussed.
summary.short_summary: Andrew Day is leading an initiative to roll up marketing agencies, aiming for an 8 million EBITDA threshold for market sale. Six agencies have expressed interest, but commitments are hindered by hesitance, creating a catch-22 situation. Substance Global, with a valuation of 2.5 million EBITDA, is the largest target and is transitioning from entertainment to pharma and wellness. Common Good, a 50-year-old family business with 1.4 million EBITDA, is wary due to legacy concerns. Imaginary Content, committed to the rollup, generates over 1 million EBITDA and focuses on digital content for craft and retail brands. The current pipeline totals around 5 million EBITDA, needing an additional 3 million to meet the target. Jon Simon is tasked with operational integration and identifying intellectual property. The holding company plans to use trigger contracts to acquire firms at 5x multiples, with equity distributed based on pro-rata valuations. Andrew Day will address emotional concerns of Common Good stakeholders before discussing financial aspects.
